outlooks.summary: Severe storms -- including potential for very large hail, along with locally damaging winds and a couple of tornadoes -- are expected this afternoon and evening from eastern parts of Oklahoma and Texas to the Mississippi Delta region. A few severe storms may also produce locally damaging winds over central Florida.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: With the exception of upper ridging progged to shift eastward across the West Coast states, the remainder of the U.S. will remain under the influence of broadly cyclonic upper flow. Embedded, subtle short-wave troughing will advance eastward across the eastern Gulf Coast Region and Florida through the day, while a more substantial short-wave trough shifts southeastward out of the Rockies and into the central/southern Plains during the afternoon. Overnight, this feature will cross the Arklatex/Ozarks, reaching the mid and lower Mississippi Valley by the end of the period. At the surface, a weakening cold front will cross the Atlantic Coast states and northern/western Gulf of Mexico. Meanwhile, a low is forecast to move eastward across Oklahoma during the day, in conjunction with the aforementioned upper trough. A trailing cold front will sweep across the southern Plains through the afternoon and evening. By the end of the period, expect the gradually deepening low to have reached southeastern Missouri/northeastern Arkansas, with the trailing front extending across the Delta region and south-southwestward into the western Gulf.

sections.title: Eastern portions of the southern Plains to the MS Delta area
sections.text: While a weak cold front will be pushed southward across the northern and western Gulf by the start of the period, low-level trajectories will turn southeasterly/easterly rather quickly, as low pressure moves across Oklahoma ahead of the advancing upper trough. While the return flow will be of an incompletely modified nature, expect at least low 60s dewpoints to gradually spread northward across east Texas and into eastern Oklahoma through the day, beneath a capping inversion. By mid to late afternoon, heating/moistening of the boundary layer beneath very steep mid-level lapse rates will result in moderate destabilization, while mixing -- enhanced in the vicinity of the advancing front -- helps to gradually erode the residual capping. By roughly 21 to 22Z, expect vigorous updrafts -- initially developing in the less-unstable air over south-central Kansas/north-central Oklahoma -- to erupt rapidly southward across eastern Oklahoma and east Texas. With the aid of rapidly increasing/veering flow with height, storms will become supercellular, with the strongest likely to become rather prolific producers of very large hail. sections.title: Central Florida
sections.text: Widespread convection is likely to be ongoing across portions of northern and central Florida, and should continue through much of the day. This complicates the forecast in terms of specific locations of potentially greater severe risk, but with the background kinematics more than sufficient for organized storms, areas where ample destabilization can occur will likely support locally severe storms -- accompanied primarily by risk for damaging winds, and very heavy rain. Expect this risk to continue through the day and into the early evening, gradually shifting southward in conjunction with slow southward advance of conglomerate convective outflow. ..Goss/Lyons.. 04/24/2020

outlooks.summary: The greatest severe-storm potential today into tonight will shift from eastern parts of Oklahoma and Texas toward the lower Mississippi Valley.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: In mid/upper levels, broadly cyclonic flow will cover most of the CONUS between the Rockies and Appalachians through the period. An embedded, initially low-amplitude perturbation is apparent in moisture-channel imagery over CO, with smaller vorticity maxima southeastward across the south-central High Plains. These features should phase into a more-coherent, strengthening shortwave trough, today, reaching south-central KS, central OK and north-central TX around 00Z. By 12Z, this perturbation should reach the Mid-South region. At the surface, 11Z analysis showed a cold front extending from a low over the Chesapeake Bay southwestward across western SC, the Fl Panhandle and the north-central Gulf. This boundary was loosely linked to a warm-frontogenetic zone over east and north TX, and in turn, to another low near CDS. The latter low will move eastward across OK today then over the Ozarks region tonight. A trailing cold front, initially over the TX South Plains region and eastern NM, will strengthen and move southeastward/eastward across west TX and central OK through the day, reaching eastern OK and northeast/ central TX by 00Z. sections.title: FL Peninsula
sections.text: An ongoing, quasi-linear complex of strong/sporadically severe thunderstorms -- with embedded LEWP/bow features and mesovortices locally concentrating the severe threat -- should shift southeastward across central FL today. Damaging gusts are that main concern, though a tornado cannot be ruled out. See the remainder of tornado watch 144 and related mesoscale discussions for the near-term threat. The convective band and associated boundary have been progressing faster and further south/east than suggested by CAMs and most synoptic guidance. However, the activity is decelerating with southward extent and becoming somewhat more zonal in alignment, more parallel to flow aloft, with additional convection expected to train across the region from the Gulf. Rich low-level moisture, with surface dew points commonly in the 70s F, will combine with diurnal heating of the upstream air mass across south-central and southern FL to boost MLCAPE into the 1500-2500 J/kg range, especially near the coasts. outlooks.summary: The greatest threat for storms with large hail, damaging winds, and a few tornadoes is expected late this afternoon into early tonight from southeast Oklahoma into the ArkLaTex region.

sections.title: Southeast OK into the ArkLaTex this evening
sections.text: A midlevel shortwave trough and associated surface cyclone will move eastward across OK this afternoon and into AR tonight, as a trailing cold front moves southeastward across TX. A narrow corridor of low-level moisture return is underway from southeast TX toward southeast OK. Though moisture is initially shallow across TX, advection and evapotranspiration beneath the cap will support boundary-layer dewpoints increasing to the low 60s into southeast OK and the mid 60s potentially into northeast TX immediately ahead of a pre-frontal trough/developing dryline. Deeper mixing along the surface trough, in tandem with low-midlevel ascent preceding the midlevel trough, should support thunderstorm initiation by late afternoon (21-22z) from eastern OK southward into northeast TX. Based on midlevel lapse rates in excess of 8 C/km in regional 12z soundings, as well as warming surface temperatures and increasing low-level moisture, a narrow corridor of moderate buoyancy (MLCAPE 1500-2500 J/kg) is expected in advance of the pre-frontal trough. Deep-layer vertical shear will favor supercells, with the stronger storms capable of producing isolated very large hail given cool midlevel temperatures

sections.title: Central/south FL this afternoon
sections.text: An outflow boundary continues to sag southward near Lake Okeechobee as of midday, with substantial clouds/rain across central FL likely to reinforce the boundary through the afternoon. There will still be a chance for isolated damaging winds with storms near and on the immediate cool side of the boundary, either as convection moves inland from the eastern Gulf, or with diurnal development inland along the wind shift. ..Thompson/Cook.. 04/24/2020

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of producing severe hail, strong wind gusts, and potential for a couple of tornadoes, are expected late this afternoon and evening across parts of the southeastern Plains into the Piney Woods and Ark-La-Tex region.

sections.title: 20Z Outlook Update
sections.text: Changes to categorical and probabilistic lines have been made, mainly to account for ongoing trends concerning convective developmen and destabilization.

sections.title: Southeastern Plains into Ark-La-Tex
sections.text: Large-scale forcing for ascent near the axis of stronger daytime heating, along/ahead of surface troughing and an associated cold front shifting eastward and southward across the southern Plains, still appears likely to contribute to an environment conducive to organized vigorous convective development late this afternoon and evening. This is expected to include a few supercells posing a risk for severe hail and strong surface gusts. Low-level hodographs probably will become supportive of potential for tornadoes, but low-level moisture return is limited, and relatively dry air in the lower/mid troposphere may result in cold outflow tending to quickly undercut the low-level mesocylones. Still, a couple of generally short-lived tornadoes may not be out of the question, particularly near a developing surface low across southeastern Oklahoma into the Ark-La-Tex region early this evening.

sections.title: Southern Florida
sections.text: An area of locally enhanced convergence near the intersection of convective outflow and the sea-breeze could still support vigorous convective development along southeast coastal areas near Miami. Other strong storms may continue to attempt to spread off the Gulf of Mexico into Gulf coastal areas between Tampa and Naples. However, weak low-level convergence across much of interior southern Florida seems to limit convective potential, in general, resulting in lowering of severe probabilities for the remainder of the afternoon. ..Kerr.. 04/24/2020 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1155 AM CDT Fri Apr 24 2020/

outlooks.summary: Severe hail, strong wind gusts, and a threat for tornadoes continues this evening across parts of eastern Oklahoma/Texas into Arkansas/Louisiana.

sections.title: 01z Update
sections.text: Early-evening water-vapor imagery depicts a well-defined short-wave trough ejecting across the southern Plains. High-level diffluent flow downstream of this feature across the Arklatex region is proving favorable for venting aloft and convection is now growing upscale ahead of the short wave. Several severe supercells have emerged along the Red River from southeastern OK into northeast TX and very large hail and tornadoes have recently been reported. 00z sounding from FWD exhibited steep low-midlevel lapse rates within a post-frontal air mass and this plume extends into northeast TX immediately ahead of the supercell cluster. It appears this activity will spread/develop east in line with earlier outlook forecasts and CAMs guidance. Farther south along the front, updrafts are slowly deepening along the front from Leon into Robertson Counties. This activity will be near the southern end of organized severe, but a more southeastward movement could allow these storms to spread into the northern part of HGX CWA. ..Darrow.. 04/25/2020

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated severe threat is expected to continue across parts of central Florida over the next couple of hours. Wind damage would be the primary threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A convective line of storms is ongoing in the southeast part of WW 144 just to the west of Melbourne, Florida. These storms are located along a gradient of moderate instability with the RAP showing MLCAPE near 2500 J/kg. The Melbourne 88D-VWP shows 0-6 km shear near 50 kt with 40 kt of flow just above the surface. This will support a severe threat as the line moves toward the coast over the next 1 to 2 hours. As surface heating takes place, new storms could develop along the outflow boundary in central Florida. Additional storms may also move inland across western Florida. The environment, characterized by moderate instability and strong low-level flow, should support a wind-damage threat with the stronger cells. Any severe threat is expected to remain isolated.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated hail and damaging wind gusts are possible with convection developing eastward across the discussion area. A WW issuance may be considered later this afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convective trends indicate gradually expanding/intensifying storms near the Wichita Metro area, with a few echoes now starting to appear in radar imagery across far north-central Oklahoma. The storms are concentrated near a north-to-south oriented surface trough near/just west of I35/135, with attendant convergence and lift from a mid-level shortwave trough approaching the region maintaining storms amidst modest instability. 7-7.5 C/km mid-level lapse rates support hail in the strongest cells, though weaknesses in flow aloft should limit the overall severe risk. A wind-damage threat may evolve with any linear segments that can develop as well. Latest CAMs/model guidance suggest that ongoing storms will persist while migrating eastward across southeastern Kansas. A few storms will also develop over time across northern Oklahoma - potentially affecting the Tulsa Metro area late afternoon. The overall risk appears to be too limited for a WW issuance in the short-term, although this will be re-evaluated as storms expand/develop southward into Oklahoma. ..Cook.. 04/24/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms may pose some threat for a few locally strong wind gusts and marginally severe hail this afternoon. Threat is expected to remain marginal, and a WW is not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: This afternoon, thunderstorms are developing across central and southeast VA in vicinity of a southeast-advancing front and in association with a progressive low amplitude shortwave trough. Diabatic heating of the surface layer with low 70s F temperatures and dewpoints around 60 F has resulted in 500-1000 J/kg MLCAPE but with weak mid-level lapse rates. Only modest vertical wind profiles with 35 kt effective bulk shear will promote mostly multicell storm modes, and a few storms may produce isolated instances of hail and locally strong wind gusts.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Though the threat is more conditional with southern extent, hail (perhaps significant) and wind gusts will become more likely with time. A few tornadoes cannot be completely ruled out. A WW is being considered this afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent observations/satellite indicate sharpening surface convergence along a trough axis located from near PNC to CQB to ADM and FTW, with areas of cumulus now apparent especially near CQB and vicinity. The environment across the warm sector has remained capped so far, though cooling aloft associated with an approaching mid-level wave should eventually result in scattered to numerous storms especially in east-central/southeastern Oklahoma. CAMs/observational guidance cast a bit of doubt on convective coverage in northeastern Texas, though at least isolated storms are expected in these areas through the evening. Steep mid-level lapse rates and impressive mid-level shear profiles (with shear vectors orthogonal to the initiating surface trough) favor supercellular development, with relatively meager boundary layer moisture being the limiting factor for a more widespread tornado threat. Nevertheless, large hail (perhaps significant near rotating updrafts) and damaging wind gusts are expected as storms develop and mature. This threat may begin to materialize as early as 21-22Z in east-central Oklahoma and expand east/southeastward over time. Given the ongoing convective trends, a Tornado Watch may be needed at some point by 22Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The greatest hail threat within WW 145 will exist with discrete activity in eastern OK into western Arkansas. The threat for damaging/severe wind gusts will increase as storms organize linearly along the advancing cold front. Deep-layer shear and upper-level forcing will remain favorable, but buoyancy will decrease this evening. A downstream severe thunderstorm watch may be needed for western/central Arkansas should convective trends warrant.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A discrete supercell within Haskell/Sequoyah Counties in Oklahoma will likely be the source of the greatest hail threat (1-2 inches possible) during the next 1-2 hours. To the west of this cell, linear development has increased along the cold front. This line of thunderstorms is likely to continue eastward for some time given the favorable large-scale ascent moving across the region. With time, storms along the front are likely to overtake any discrete activity out ahead of it where the threats will primarily become damaging/severe wind gusts and marginally severe hail. The main uncertainty is how severe the storms along the front will be as they progress into western/central Arkansas over the next few hours. Upper-level forcing and effective shear (40-50 kts) will remain favorable; however, buoyancy will tend to decrease with time as the boundary layer cools. MLCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg will be possible this evening. A downstream severe thunderstorm watch may be needed in portions of central Arkansas. Convective trends will be monitored. ..Wendt.. 04/24/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe/tornado threat is increasing, particularly across northern parts of the watch in the short term.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms have been slow to develop across the WW area, with entrainment issues apparent per visible satellite imagery. However, robust storm development is now underway near the Red River west/northwest of Paris TX. Here, a mesolow is analyzed in the Johnston County OK vicinity along the advancing surface front, with low-level flow backed across the valley area to the east. Several deep/rotating updrafts are rapidly evolving in this area, with a tornado recently reported near Paris, along with 2" hail. Very large hail is expected across northern parts of the watch over the next 1-2 hours, along with locally damaging winds and continued tornado potential, as these storms likely continue/spread east-southeastward with time. Other storm development is still expected southward -- both near and ahead of the front -- over the next hour or so, per consistent CAM guidance and persistent, congested cumulus per visible imagery. All-hazard severe risk would exist with any storms which develop. ..Goss.. 04/25/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Risk for large hail and locally damaging winds will continue to increase over parts of east/southeast Texas and into northern and central Louisiana. A new WW may be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest visible satellite imagery shows storms developing southwestward along the east Texas cold front -- with new development near and just south of the southern edge of Tornado Watch 146. Meanwhile, couple of new updrafts are initiating over northern Louisiana, and with time, expect the ongoing east Texas storms to spread eastward into/across northern and central Louisiana. Evening RAOBs and RAP-based objective analysis show ample instability (mixed-layer CAPE 1000 to 1500 J/kg), and shear favorable for supercells. As such, potential for large hail and damaging winds -- and possibly a tornado -- should evolve and persist well into the evening, especially over parts of Louisiana east of Tornado Watch 146. ..Goss.. 04/25/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe risk -- including potential for destructive winds and very large hail -- continues across parts of northeast Texas and adjacent northwestern Louisiana.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest radar loop shows several supercell storms over the northwestern Louisiana vicinity, with one large cell crossing the Cass/Marion County Texas and Caddo County Louisiana border area suggestive of destructive wind gust potential, along with very large hail. Inbound velocities per the KSHV WSR-88D in the RFD region of this cell are in the 60 to 70 kt range at roughly 1500 feet AGL, and so wind gusts well in excess of 60 MPH are expected. With time, expect continued evolution toward damaging wind potential -- including a possible bow echo evolution -- as storms move across northwestern Louisiana and eventually into WW 147. ..Goss.. 04/25/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe risk -- increasingly in the form of locally damaging winds -- continues.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several clusters of strong/severe storms continue moving east-southeastward across Arkansas and northern/central Louisiana. While storms across Arkansas continue to gradually evolve into a cohesive band, northern Louisiana convection has maintained a more persistently cellular structure thus far. Still, expect upscale growth into clusters/bands to occur across this region as well, over the next 1-2 hours. At this time, the most intense storm has passed just northeast of Shreveport, where large hail and damaging winds are indicated by radar. With time, storms will approach the current eastern bounds of the watch into central Louisiana and also across northern Arkansas. However, limited and decreasing buoyancy with eastern extent may preclude the need for new WW issuance east of the watch. ..Goss.. 04/25/2020 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
